beats.say: Now you are the seller. You are selling an old pram on a classifieds site for 260 manat.
The buyer writes that she has already paid, and asks you to open this link to receive the money.

body.text: Hi, I'll take the pram! I paid through AlSat Safe Deal.
To receive the money, confirm your card here:

beats.say: Receiving money needs only the card number. The three digits on the back and the text code are never needed.
If such a link arrives, type nothing. Talk to the buyer only in the site's own messages.

scenes.prompt: Find the warning signs on this page.

body.text: The buyer has paid 260.00 AZN. Confirm your card to receive the money.
Enter card number, expiry date and CVV
Enter the SMS code from your bank
The deal will be cancelled in 15 minutes

spots.label: Strange address
spots.explain: This is not the classifieds site's own address. A familiar name was added to a different domain.

spots.label: Code on the back of the card
spots.explain: This code is for taking money out of your card. It is never needed to receive money.

spots.label: SMS code
spots.explain: The text message code confirms a payment. If you type it, money leaves your card.

spots.label: Pressure
spots.explain: The countdown is there to stop you thinking. A real site does not rush the seller.

scenes.title: The buyer's link
scenes.intro: You opened the link the buyer sent. In the browser, choose the right move at every step.

steps.label: Money is waiting for you: 260.00 AZN

actions.label: Receive money
actions.feedback: This button does not pay you, it opens a form that asks for card details. The address is not the classifieds site.

actions.label: Close tab
actions.feedback: Right. The address was strange, so type nothing on that page.

actions.label: Open the site myself
actions.feedback: Well done. When you open the site yourself, you do not land on a fake page.

steps.say: The form also wants the code on the back of the card.

actions.label: Confirm
actions.feedback: With these details the scammer can pay from your card. This code is not needed to receive money.

actions.label: Cancel
actions.feedback: Right. A page that asks for the code on the back of the card does not give money, it takes it.

body.text: Your bank sent a 6 digit code.
Do not worry if the SMS says "payment": this is a receiving transaction.

steps.say: The bank message says payment, but the page says receipt.

actions.label: Confirm code
actions.feedback: The code approved a payment and money left your card. Call your bank right away.

actions.label: Cancel
actions.feedback: Right. The text message code is for payments, so never type it on a page or give it to anyone.

steps.label: AlSat: messages with the buyer
steps.say: This is the classifieds site itself.

actions.label: Report buyer
actions.feedback: Well done. The site will close the scam account and protect other sellers.

actions.label: Write to buyer: cash when we meet
actions.feedback: Good. Meeting and taking cash is the simplest and safest way.

actions.label: Send a photo of both sides of the card
actions.feedback: The photo also shows the code on the back. That means handing your card to the scammer.

question.prompt: The buyer wants to transfer money to your card. What is enough to give?

options.label: Only the card number or account number
options.feedback: Right. Nothing else is needed to receive money.

options.label: Card number, expiry date and the code on the back
options.feedback: With these details someone can pay from your card. Never give the code on the back.

options.label: The SMS code from the bank
options.feedback: The text message code is for taking money out. A buyer who asks for it is a scammer.

options.label: A photo of both sides of the card
options.feedback: The photo holds everything, including the code on the back. It is like handing over the card.

scenes.explain: Receiving money never needs the code on the back of the card or a text message code. Anyone who asks for them is a scammer.

nodes.text: In a hurry you typed your card details and the SMS code. A minute later the bank texts you: 389 manat has left your card.

choices.label: Call the bank at once on the number on the card and block it
choices.feedback: Right. Blocking the card quickly stops further payments.

choices.label: Write to the buyer and ask for the money back
choices.feedback: The scammer will not pay it back, and time is passing. Call the bank first.

choices.label: I feel ashamed and tell no one
choices.feedback: Silence gives the scammer time. Banks and police deal with cases like this every day.

nodes.text: Your card is blocked. What else would you like to do?
nodes.speaker: Gulnar (bank operator)
nodes.spoken: Your card is blocked. <breath> What else would you like to do?

choices.label: Save screenshots and report to the police and the classifieds site
choices.feedback: Well done. Evidence helps the police, and the site closes the scam account.

choices.label: Delete the chat so I can forget it
choices.feedback: The chat is evidence. Do not delete it, show it to the police.

points: Receiving money never needs the code on the back of the card or an SMS code.
Type nothing into a payment link a buyer sends you.
If you typed a code, call your bank at once on the number on the card.
